newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Estate says RGI becomes its 100% unit.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Estate says RGI becomes its 100% unit.

text.p: Mitsubishi Estate Co Ltd said on Friday that it had acquired an additional 20 percent stake in Rockefeller Group Inc (RGI) of the United States for about $151 million, making RGI Mitsubishi's wholly-owned unit.

It said RGI is now making profits after transferring ownership of 12 buildings at Rockefeller Center to Rockefeller Center Properties Inc in exchange for a $1.3 billion mortgage on the New York landmark.

The Japanese property giant, which first agreed in 1989 to pay $846 million for a 51 percent stake in RGI, owned 80 percent of the U.S. company by 1991 while the Rockefeller Family Trusts owned the other 20 percent.
The purchase of RGI shares on Friday was made at the request of the Rockefeller Family Trust, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
Last March, Mitsubishi Estate saw a 1995/96 net loss of 122 billion yen, mainly from the write-off of its investment in the Rockefeller properties.
RGI currently owns 100 percent of the Time & Life Building and a 55 percent interest in the McGraw Hill Building in New York.
